title: Deadly 7.7 Earthquake Kills 38 in Indonesia as Second Quake Strikes Sumatra Hours Later
excerpt: Hospitals, schools, and homes damaged across Flores island as twin earthquakes rattled Indonesia on Saturday, prompting evacuations and a brief tsunami warning.
body:
• A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Indonesia's Flores island on Saturday, killing at least 38 people and damaging hospitals, schools, and over 50 homes
  • A separate 6.4-magnitude quake hit North Sumatra hours later, though no immediate casualties were reported from the second event
  • Around 2,000 residents were evacuated and a tsunami warning was briefly issued before being lifted after waves up to 1 meter were recorded
  • Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has suffered several devastating quakes in recent decades, including the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami

Twin Quakes Shake Indonesia

A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Flores island in Indonesia's East Nusa Tenggara province early Saturday morning, killing at least 38 people and triggering widespread panic across the archipelago. Hours later, a separate 6.4-magnitude quake hit North Sumatra province, compounding fears in a nation that sits squarely on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

The initial earthquake struck around 6 a.m. local time, about 68 kilometers northwest of Ende, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency BNPB confirmed two people sustained serious injuries and 11 suffered minor injuries, in addition to the 38 fatalities.

Widespread Damage Across Flores

Healthcare facilities, schools, government offices, and more than 50 homes were damaged in the earthquake, BNPB said. Videos posted on social media showed buildings collapsing as panicked residents ran screaming through dust-filled streets. One video captured severe damage to a hospital in the village of Aeramo.

At the Roman Catholic St. Peter Major Seminary in the coastal village of Sikka, the roof of an assembly hall collapsed during morning Mass, forcing students and nuns to flee in panic, according to the Associated Press. At least one priest suffered a broken leg after jumping from the second floor during the quake, the seminary's rector Rev. Guidelbertus Tanga said.

"Although I have experienced several earthquakes on Flores island before, this was by far the strongest and longest earthquake I have ever experienced."

— Theresia Uta, 52, resident of Maumere

Tsunami Warning Briefly Issued

A tsunami warning was initially issued but later lifted after waves up to 1 meter high were recorded in Maurole, Ende, according to Indonesia's meteorology agency BMKG. Around 2,000 residents of Nagekeo regency were evacuated as a precautionary measure.

BNPB deployed a helicopter along with its emergency response team, noting that the landscape of the area — consisting of many islands — makes access challenging. The national search and rescue agency shared footage of workers digging through rubble, searching for possible survivors.

Second Quake Hits North Sumatra

The second earthquake, initially measured at 6.4 magnitude, struck at a depth of 168 kilometers in North Sumatra province, with its epicenter located about 11 kilometers southeast of Simalungun. BMKG said the quake was felt by residents in Tebing Tinggi, Kabanjahe, and Limapuluh areas but reported no tsunami threat or immediate damage.

A Nation on the Ring of Fire

Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, is one of the most seismically active countries in the world. The catastrophic 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, triggered by a 9.1-magnitude earthquake off Sumatra, killed more than 220,000 people along coastlines across the Indian Ocean, more than half of them in Indonesia.

Flores island, known for its colorful volcanic lakes and as a gateway to Komodo National Park, is home to roughly 2 million people spread across small villages. The island's remote terrain is expected to complicate rescue and relief operations in the coming days.
